PICS: Four-bed house for €220k in Waterford - oh, and it comes with its own church

Quite the conversation starter with your new neighbours

  • Bookmark
  • Share
  • Comments1
News
By
Thomas Lawrance
  • 14:07, 13 OCT 2026
  • Bookmark
    • Listen to audio version of this article
    Sponsored by
    0:00 / 1:34
    Instaread

    The average price of a semi-D in Cork city now stands at around €400,000, but for just over half of that, you could net this stunning 19th century home - plus the disused old church next door.

    The Manse in Coolfinn, Portlaw, Co. Waterford dates back to the 1840s, and has plenty of its own garden space along with four bedrooms, some very charming interior design and all the mod cons you'll need in the 2020s. It's also just an hour's drive from Mark Zuckerberg's new neighbourhood, with this stretch of the country fast becoming the place to be.

    But while Meta boss Zuckerberg shelled out an eye-watering €51 million for Strancally Castle, the Manse could be yours for €220,000. Up for sale with Sherry FitzGerald John Rohan, the property is nestled in the village of Portlaw, 19km from Waterford city.

    A four-bed home backing onto a river might sound attractive enough, but it's the church tower in the garden that will be the real conversation starter at your housewarming party.

    Sherry Fitzgerald explained: "ne of the property's most distinctive features is the adjoining former church building, dating from circa 1845. While the church is currently in need of repair, it presents an exceptional opportunity for future development or alternative use, subject to the necessary planning permissions and statutory consents."
